report:
## Evidence on CoQ10 for Statin-Related Muscle Symptoms

The evidence is genuinely mixed, so "yes" is only partially supported.

**Supporting benefit:** A 2018 meta-analysis in the *Journal of the American Heart Association* (12 RCTs) found CoQ10 supplementation "ameliorated statin-associated muscle symptoms, such as muscle pain, muscle weakness, muscle cramps, and muscle tiredness" (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/full/10.1161/JAHA.118.009835). A more recent (2024/2025) systematic review and meta-analysis similarly reported that CoQ10 (50 mg twice daily) was "associated with improvement in statin-associated muscle symptoms, reflected by lower pain scores and reduced creatine kinase levels" (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12536858/).

**Against benefit:** Other rigorous reviews reach the opposite conclusion. A 2020 systematic review/meta-analysis in *Atherosclerosis* (7 RCTs) concluded the analysis "did not favour the use of CoQ10" for statin-associated myalgia, though it was limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneity (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021915020301386). A 2021 meta-analysis in the *Irish Journal of Medical Science* likewise found "supplementation with CoQ10 did not have any significant benefit in improving statin-induced myopathy" (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11845-021-02651-x). Individual placebo-controlled RCTs (e.g., a randomized double-blind study by Taylor et al.) also found no significant reduction in myalgia versus placebo.

**Conclusion:** The claim that CoQ10 relieves statin-related muscle discomfort is not firmly established. Some meta-analyses report modest benefit, but these are offset by equally rigorous reviews finding no effect, with authors citing small trials, short duration, heterogeneous dosing, and inconsistent outcome measures as key limitations. Overall, the evidence is inconclusive rather than a clear "yes"—CoQ10 may help some patients but is not proven effective across the population, and current guidelines do not strongly endorse it for this purpose.
